5-7.3.2 Cleaning and Passivation Procedures.
In the startup of new cooling tower systems containing complex metallurgies that
include galvanized steel, follow the cleaning and passivation procedures for cooling
tower systems containing galvanized steel, stainless steel, mild steel, or copper. These
procedures should not be used for cleaning and passivating aluminum. Conventional
chemical cleaners and typical heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) water
treatment programs use highly alkaline, high-pH water, which can initiate white rust
formation on galvanized surfaces and copper tubes. Galvanized steel can simply be
passivated by exposure to highly aerated water and a phosphate or polysilicate
treatment. This treatment forms a zinc corrosion inhibition layer, which is a natural,
dense, adherent, and protective corrosion product film. High pH (above 8.5) produces
unwanted white rust that is fragile and not protective against corrosion. The following
procedures are recommended.
5-7.3.2.1 Hydrostatic Testing.
Perform hydrostatic testing:
a. Inspect and remove all debris.
b. Fill the system with treated water and circulate. This should include
orthophosphate or hexametaphosphate (as PO ) at 40 to 60 ppm, and
4
tolyltriazole (active) at 10 to 20 ppm.
5-7.3.2.2 Pre-operational Cleaning Procedure.
If the system passes hydrostatic testing, proceed immediately to this pre-operational
cleaning and passivation procedure. Do not allow untreated water to be added to the
system.
a. Drain and flush any debris from hydrostatic testing.
b. Dose and circulate (for 24 hours) a sufficient amount of a cleaning formula
based on the volume of the system. A formulation is provided below.
c. Drain and flush the system, and clean all strainers.
d. Fill the system with makeup water and circulate for 30 minutes.
e. Take a sample of system water while it is circulating. The sample should
match the makeup water supply for clarity and SS; conductivity ±10 percent;
and pH ±0.3 pH units from 7.5 to 8.5.
If necessary, repeat steps a) through e) until the system water matches this description.
The system should now be clean and passivated.
5-7.3.2.3 Chemical Cleaning and Passivation Formulation.
Apply this chemical cleaning and passivation formulation when the water system pH is
7.5 to 8.5; adjust pH as required. Formulation limitations may require adding separate
components to keep things in solution. Other formulations may be used.

### 2. EXECUTION NARRATIVE (per circuit, per stage)
Each circuit follows the same seven-stage sequence. HYDRO is owed only where CX-02 has no accepted chart on file (01 91 13 cl.1.3): the hydrostatic charts TR-0414/0416/0417/0418 cited for C3, C5, C6 and C7 are not in the commissioning records, so those four circuits are re-tested at 127.5 psig for 120 min with the lump-sum hydrostatic test pump (the flush skids cannot reach test pressure and are not intended to, 23 25 16 cl.3.10f). C1, C2, C4 and C8 are recorded PASS with charts TR-0412/0413/0415/0419 on file and are not re-tested (23 21 16 cl.3.3); their HYDRO rows are filed at zero duration and no water.

**INITIAL_FLUSH** — one full circuit displacement (n_f = 1) at the declared flow with the 40-mesh (380 µm) temporary strainer in each skid discharge and the temporary bypass spools fitted to every M-602 component that has a bypass provision (C2–C7). Bypassed components are isolated from construction debris.

**CHEM_CLEAN** — the cleaner scheduled for the circuit's metallurgy in VD-06 is dosed on the SYSTEM volume at the volumetric application rate (CL-100 1.5 gal/1000 gal for carbon/copper steel; CL-210 2.0 gal/1000 gal for the galvanized riser C8 and the aluminium cold-plate circuit C6, which cannot take high pH — UFC cl.10-1.1, VD-04). The polyacrylate dispersant PD-45 is carried at 5 ppm active (UFC cl.5-3.7). The charge is circulated for 24 h (UFC cl.5-7.3.2.2b), then drained and the strainers cleaned. Spent cleaner from C4–C8 carries copper/zinc taken up from copper pipe/galvanizing (VD-06 Note 3) and is hauled to a permitted facility; C1–C3 spent cleaner is sewered.

**DRAIN_RINSE** — n_r full circuit-volume displacements computed from the project rinse model C_n = C_mk + (C0 − C_mk)·exp(−η·n) until the rinse endpoint of UFC cl.5-7.3.2.2 is met (conductivity ≤ 1.1·C_mk and pH 7.5–8.5). C_mk (makeup conductivity) and the spent-solution conductivities C0 are read from SW-02 and VD-06 Note 3 (see §6 on the unreadable scans). The circuit is left full at the last displacement, so rinse effluent is one displacement less than the rinse draw. Bypass spools remain fitted through the rinse so the protected components are not flushed and are filled later at turnover.

**PASSIVATE** — the passivation inhibitor of UFC Table 5-11 is dosed on the SYSTEM volume into the water standing at the end of the rinse and circulated one displacement plus 30 min to distribute (UFC cl.5-7.3.2.2d). Molybdate (50 ppm Mo, 10–12 day film) is used for the carbon/copper-steel circuits (C1–C5, C7); polysilicate (50 ppm SiO2, 10–12 day film) for the aluminium circuit C6 and the galvanized riser C8 (aluminium and galvanized cannot take pH > 8.5). Tolyltriazole at 10 ppm is carried wherever copper is wetted (C4–C7). Soda ash (SA-100) adjusts the molybdate circuits to pH 8.5–9.5. pH is controlled to the intersection of the bands where two inhibitors are carried (C4–C7).
